evals.name: explicit-request-launches
evals.prompt: /continue-in-background — I'm heading out for the evening; pick the work up in a background agent. The working tree is clean apart from the handoff save-points. Done when the test suite passes and the work is committed.
evals.expected_output: The skill produces the save-point via the shared engine, emits the rails resume prompt, passes the dirty-tree gate (only save-point files under the handoff location), launches a fresh background agent seeded with the `/goal` payload (claude --bg --name continue-<topic>), reports the launch result with the claude agents management hint and any non-inherited configuration worth flagging, and STOPS — it does not monitor the launched agent.
expectations: A save-point is produced per the shared engine doc and the rails resume prompt is emitted first (transparency + manual fallback)
The dirty-tree gate runs git status --porcelain -uall and exempts only save-point files under the handoff location
A background agent is launched with the `/goal` payload (the stated done condition as its goal) via claude --bg and the launch result is reported, replacing the /clear-then-paste instruction

The claude --bg launch command carries --permission-mode auto, and the report states that auto mode may deny an action and that where a denied action is reported is unverified; a report that says nothing about denied actions fails, and so does one that promises they appear in the launched session's final hand-off
The report surfaces launched-session behavior: the agent is a NEW session that inherits neither the current session's CLI flags nor its model/effort choices
The skill STOPS after the launch report — no monitoring, polling, or new work items

evals.name: no-explicit-intent-no-launch
evals.prompt: I'm heading out, context is heavy — checkpoint this so nothing is lost.
evals.expected_output: The user asked for a checkpoint, not background delegation, so the hard gate blocks the launch: the skill produces the save-point and the rails resume prompt with the standard /clear-then-paste instruction, states that no background agent was launched because background delegation was not explicitly requested, and STOPS.
expectations: The skill does NOT launch a background agent (no claude --bg invocation) — going AFK with heavy context is not explicit background-delegation intent
The exit is the save-point plus the copy/paste resume prompt with a /clear-then-paste instruction
The response states that background launch was withheld for lack of an explicit request, and how to request it
The skill does not self-elect the launch even though the user is going AFK

evals.name: dirty-tree-falls-back
evals.prompt: /continue-in-background — keep the work moving while I'm away. (Note: the working tree has unrelated uncommitted edits in src/other-feature.ts from a different task.) Done when the test suite passes and the work is committed.
evals.expected_output: The dirty-tree gate detects unrelated uncommitted changes (outside save-point files under the handoff location) and does NOT launch the background agent — those edits would not carry into the isolated worktree the background session moves into before editing. It reports why and falls back to the standard /clear-then-paste instruction, noting the user can commit or stash and re-run /continue-in-background.
expectations: The skill runs the dirty-tree gate with git status --porcelain -uall (the -uall is required — default porcelain collapses untracked directories and can hide unrelated dirt behind the exempt handoff directory) and ignores only save-point files under the handoff location, not the unrelated src/other-feature.ts edits
It does NOT launch the background agent because unrelated uncommitted changes are present (and it is not already inside a linked worktree)
It reports the reason and falls back to the standard /clear-then-paste instruction, noting the user can commit or stash and re-run /continue-in-background

evals.name: linked-worktree-dirty-tree-launches
evals.prompt: /continue-in-background — take it from here, I'm off for the night. (Note: this session is already running inside a linked git worktree created with git worktree add, and the tree has uncommitted edits from the current task.) Done when the test suite passes and the work is committed.
evals.expected_output: The dirty-tree gate's linked-worktree exception applies: background sessions skip worktree isolation when already inside a linked worktree, so the uncommitted edits stay visible to the launched agent. The skill launches the background agent despite the dirty tree, reports the launch result, and STOPS.
expectations: The skill launches the background agent even though the tree has uncommitted changes, because the current session already runs inside a linked git worktree (the documented exception — isolation is skipped there, so the edits remain visible to the launched agent)
It does NOT fall back to /clear-then-paste on account of the dirty tree
The launch result is reported and the skill STOPS — no monitoring or babysitting

evals.name: non-repo-directory-launches
evals.prompt: /continue-in-background — I'm done for the night, hand it to a background agent. (Note: this session was started in my home directory, which is not a git repository at all — git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree fails with 'fatal: not a git repository' — and no WorktreeCreate hook is configured in any settings scope that applies here.) Done when the test suite passes and the work is committed.
evals.expected_output: The dirty-tree gate identifies the consuming directory as not a git repository — not merely a failed command — and establishes that no WorktreeCreate hook is configured, so the non-repo branch applies: there is no uncommitted work to protect and no worktree isolation to lose, because the background session writes to the working directory directly. It launches the background agent, states that reading in the launch report, and STOPS.
expectations: The skill establishes repository status first (git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree) rather than running git status --porcelain -uall blind and stalling on 'fatal: not a git repository'
It identifies the non-repo case positively AND establishes that no WorktreeCreate hook is configured before launching the background agent
The launch report states the non-repo reading: no uncommitted work to protect, and the launched session writes to the working directory directly instead of moving into an isolated worktree
The skill STOPS after the launch report — no monitoring, polling, or new work items

evals.name: unknown-tree-state-does-not-launch
evals.prompt: /continue-in-background — keep it moving, I'm away. (Note: git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree exits non-zero with 'fatal: detected dubious ownership in repository at ...' — this IS a repository, git just refuses to read it.) Done when the test suite passes and the work is committed.
evals.expected_output: The gate's third branch applies: git failed for a reason other than 'not a git repository', so the tree's state is unknown rather than clean. The skill does NOT launch — it reports the git failure and falls back to the standard /clear-then-paste instruction, exactly as it does for a dirty tree.
expectations: The skill does NOT treat a non-zero exit as the non-repo branch — the failure is not 'not a git repository', so the tree may be dirty and cannot be proven clean
It does NOT launch the background agent: unknown tree state is handled like dirty state, not like clean state
It reports what the command said and falls back to the standard /clear-then-paste instruction

evals.name: no-work-tree-despite-zero-exit-does-not-launch
evals.prompt: /continue-in-background — hand this to a background agent, I'm off. (Note: the working directory is a bare repository, so git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree exits 0 and prints 'false'.) Done when the test suite passes and the work is committed.
evals.expected_output: A zero exit is not evidence of a clean tree. The command printed 'false', not 'true', and this is not the positively-identified non-repo case either, so it lands in the gate's unknown default: the skill does NOT launch, reports that there is no work tree to inspect, and falls back to the standard /clear-then-paste instruction.
expectations: The skill does NOT read the zero exit status as a passing gate — the printed value is 'false', so there is no work tree and nothing was proven clean
It does NOT take the non-repo launch branch either: 'false' is not the 'not a git repository' identification, so the permissive branch does not apply
It does NOT launch the background agent, and falls back to the standard /clear-then-paste instruction with the reason reported

evals.name: non-repo-with-worktreecreate-hook-does-not-launch
evals.prompt: /continue-in-background — I'm heading out, hand it to a background agent. (Note: this is a Mercurial checkout, so git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree fails with 'fatal: not a git repository', but settings.json defines WorktreeCreate and WorktreeRemove hooks so sessions get isolation without Git. I have uncommitted hg changes here.) Done when the test suite passes and the work is committed.
evals.expected_output: 'Not a git repository' alone does not open the launch branch. A configured WorktreeCreate hook is the non-Git isolation path, so the launched session moves into a hook-created workspace that this checkout's local changes never reach — the same loss the dirty-tree gate exists to prevent. The case lands in the gate's unknown default: the skill does NOT launch, reports why, and falls back to the standard /clear-then-paste instruction.
expectations: The skill does NOT launch merely because git rev-parse reported 'not a git repository' — it checks whether a WorktreeCreate hook is configured before taking that branch
It recognizes that a configured WorktreeCreate hook means the launched session works in an isolated workspace, so uncommitted local changes would not carry into it
It does NOT launch the background agent, and falls back to the standard /clear-then-paste instruction with the reason reported
An inability to establish the hook's absence is treated the same way — unknown, not clean, no launch

evals.name: position-panel-emitted-but-never-sent-to-the-agent
evals.prompt: /continue-in-background — phase 2 of 4 is wired and green, phase 3 is next. Clean tree. I'm heading out, keep it moving. Done when the test suite passes and the work is committed.
evals.expected_output: The response leads with the 'You are here' position panel (vertical rail, current phase marked, completeness line, three one-line blocks), then the rails prompt, then the launch report. The text handed to the launched agent is exactly the `/goal` payload: `/goal`, a space, and the goal region's between-rails text. No panel text travels with it.
expectations: A 'You are here' position panel is emitted, and it leads the response, ahead of the rails prompt
The rail is vertical with one phase per line and the current phase marked in the gutter
The prompt passed to the launched agent is exactly `/goal`, a space, and the goal region's between-rails text; no panel line is included in it
The rails prompt is still emitted on screen before the launch, so a refused or failed launch leaves a usable manual fallback
The reasoning treats the panel as being for the departing operator, not for the agent; the agent's payload is the same goal-region paste a person would make

evals.name: full-path-payload-is-the-emit-output
evals.prompt: /continue-in-background file phase-4 — clean tree apart from the save-points, take it from here while I'm out. Done when the test suite passes and the work is committed.
evals.expected_output: The done condition stated in the request is a fresh goal, so the full path produces a shape-2 file through `save_point.py new` with a goal region, fills the slots, and runs `save_point.py validate` to exit 0 before anything launches, with no draft and no confirmation round. The text written to the temporary prompt file for `claude --bg` is `/goal`, a space, then the between-rails text of the goal region of the `save_point.py emit <file>` output (the condition, ending with the `Read @` directive), taken from that output rather than retyped. The rails are still shown on screen first, the launch is reported, and the skill stops.
expectations: `save_point.py validate` is run and exits 0 before the background launch; a file that fails validation (including an unfinished skeleton with `<!-- FILL` slots) is never launched from
The done condition stated in the request is used as the goal, with no drafted condition and no confirmation question before the launch

The prompt handed to `claude --bg` is `/goal`, a space, and the goal region's between-rails text from the `save_point.py emit` output, written to a temporary file with the Write tool, not a retyped or paraphrased version of it

The launched payload ends with the `Read @` directive line and contains no panel text, no copy instruction, no rails, no below-rail line, and none of the resume region's `Prior session:`, `Handoff origin:` or `Next:` lines
The rails block is still emitted on screen before the launch, the launch result is reported, and the skill STOPS

evals.name: payload-arms-the-active-goal
evals.prompt: /continue-in-background file phase-5 — a /goal is active in this session and the tree is clean apart from the save-points. Take it from here while I'm out.
evals.expected_output: The full path produces a shape-2 file whose `## Resume prompt` section holds a goal region (headed by the `Type /goal` instruction) and a resume region. `save_point.py validate` exits 0 before anything launches. The temporary prompt file for `claude --bg` holds `/goal`, a space, then the goal region's between-rails text taken from the `save_point.py emit` output: the condition, ending with the `Read @` directive line. It holds no instruction line, no rails, and none of the resume region's other lines. The report tells the user to run `/goal clear` in this session, the launch is reported, and the skill stops.
expectations: `save_point.py validate` is run and exits 0 before the background launch

The prompt file handed to `claude --bg` is written with the Write tool and begins with `/goal ` followed by the goal region's condition text from the `save_point.py emit` output, not a retyped version
The payload's last line is the `Read @` directive line, byte for byte the resume region's first line
The payload contains no rails, no `Type /goal` instruction line, no `/clear`, then copy line, and no `Prior session:`, `Handoff origin:` or `Next:` line from the resume region
The report tells the user to run `/goal clear` in this session, because the active goal would keep starting turns here
The launch result is reported and the skill STOPS

evals.name: resumed-verify-launch-passes-effort-from-table
evals.prompt: /continue-in-background — the fix is implemented and committed; what remains is the verify stage: run the suite and confirm the outcome against the plan's acceptance criteria. Clean tree apart from the save-points. I'm heading out. Done when the test suite passes and the work is committed.
evals.expected_output: Because the resumed task is verify work and runs unattended, the skill reads model-config's 'Choose an effort level' table at launch, picks the level whose described use fits verification work, and passes that level as `--effort` in the `claude --bg` command. The launch report names the level and quotes the matched use. The level is taken from the live table, not from memory, and is not below medium.
expectations: The `claude --bg` launch command carries an `--effort` flag with a single level name, placed before the prompt argument
The level comes from reading model-config's 'Choose an effort level' table during this run, not from a remembered or hard-coded value
The launch report names the level passed and quotes the matched use from the table
The level passed for this verify task is not below medium
The launch result is reported and the skill STOPS

evals.name: cloud-unpushed-commits-no-launch
evals.prompt: /continue-in-background --cloud prompt — run the rest in a cloud session. The tree is clean but I have two local commits I haven't pushed. Done when the test suite passes and the work is committed.
evals.expected_output: The skill produces the save-point and rails prompt, then finds unpushed commits on the branch. Because the cloud VM clones the pushed branch, it does not run claude --cloud; it reports why, names commit-and-push as the fix, and falls back to the /clear-then-paste instruction.
expectations: The unpushed-commit check runs before any launch, after a git fetch refreshes the tracking ref
claude --cloud is not run
The report says the cloud session would not see the unpushed commits and names pushing as the fix
The fallback is the standard /clear-then-paste instruction

evals.name: cloud-without-user-ask-launches-locally
evals.prompt: Continue this in the background while I grab lunch. (The model invokes the skill with arguments: --cloud prompt) Done when the test suite passes and the work is committed.
evals.expected_output: The user asked for background work but never asked for a cloud session, so the skill drops the model-supplied --cloud and takes the local delivery: it produces the save-point and rails prompt and launches a local claude --bg session, not claude --cloud.
expectations: claude --cloud is not run
The skill treats the background request as not covering a cloud launch
The local background delivery runs instead

evals.name: cloud-default-full-path-no-launch
evals.prompt: /continue-in-background --cloud — run the rest of this plan in a cloud session. The tree is clean and pushed; the work is backed by a PLAN.md in my memory folder. Done when the test suite passes and the work is committed.
evals.expected_output: The save-point engine takes the full path by default because a plan backs the work. A handoff file in the memory tier never reaches the cloud session, so the skill does not run claude --cloud; it tells the user to commit and push the handoff or plan and rerun with --cloud prompt and a purpose naming its repo-relative path, and it commits nothing itself.
expectations: The save-point takes the full path without the user forcing it
claude --cloud is not run
The report names committing and pushing the handoff or plan, then rerunning with --cloud prompt and its repo-relative path, as the route
The skill does not commit anything

evals.name: cloud-unattended-launch-passes-effort
evals.prompt: /continue-in-background --cloud prompt fix-flaky-test — run the flaky-test fix unattended in a cloud session. The tree is clean and the branch matches origin. Done when the test suite passes and the work is committed.
evals.expected_output: The skill fetches, confirms HEAD matches the upstream, and launches claude --cloud with the prompt file and an --effort level taken from the model-config table, placed before the prompt argument and not below medium. If the CLI rejects --effort with --cloud, it relaunches without it and the report tells the user to send /effort <level> in the session. The report gives the session id, the teleport and follow-up commands and the signed-in account.
expectations: git fetch runs before HEAD is compared with the upstream
claude --cloud carries --effort with a single level name, not below medium, before the prompt argument
Only if the CLI rejects --effort with --cloud does the skill relaunch without it and advise /effort in the report
The report names the session id, the teleport and follow-up commands, and the signed-in account

evals.name: bgisolation-none-dirty-tree-launches-with-warning
evals.prompt: /continue-in-background — keep the work moving while I'm away. (Note: the working tree has unrelated uncommitted edits in src/other-feature.ts from a different task, this session is not in a linked worktree, and the project's .claude/settings.json sets "worktree": {"bgIsolation": "none"}.) Done when the test suite passes and the work is committed.
evals.expected_output: The dirty-tree gate reads the effective `worktree.bgIsolation` before judging the unrelated edits and finds `none`, so the background session will edit this checkout in place rather than in an isolated worktree, and the unrelated edits stay visible to it. The skill launches the background agent despite the dirty tree, and the launch report warns that the launched session edits this checkout in place alongside the user and states that the read did not cover a `--settings` value. The skill then STOPS.
expectations: The skill reads `worktree.bgIsolation` from the settings files before judging the unrelated src/other-feature.ts edits, and finds `none` in the project's .claude/settings.json
It launches the background agent despite the unrelated uncommitted changes, and does NOT fall back to /clear-then-paste on account of the dirty tree
The launch report warns that the launched session edits this checkout in place, alongside the user, not in an isolated worktree
The launch report states that the settings read did not cover a `--settings` value
The skill STOPS after the launch report — no monitoring, polling, or new work items

evals.name: no-goal-drafts-a-condition-and-asks
evals.prompt: /continue-in-background file phase-6 — keep going on the remaining steps while I'm out. Clean tree apart from the save-points. No /goal is set in this session and I have not said what done looks like.
evals.expected_output: No goal applies, so the skill drafts a checkable completion condition from the remaining work with /planning:draft-goal-condition, writes the save-point with it as a fresh goal so the condition appears on screen as the goal region, then asks the user to confirm the launch with that condition. It launches nothing this turn: the original request was made before the condition was shown, so it is not approval to arm it.
expectations: A completion condition is drafted through /planning:draft-goal-condition, or by following that skill's procedure, from the save-point's remaining work
The drafted condition appears on screen as the save-point's goal region before any launch
The skill asks the user to confirm the launch with that condition
No `claude --bg` command runs this turn; the original invocation is not treated as approval of a condition the user had not seen

evals.name: no-checkable-condition-refuses-launch
evals.prompt: /continue-in-background — what's left is to watch the deploy dashboard every 10 minutes and ping me if anything changes. Clean tree apart from the save-points. No /goal is set in this session. I'm heading out.
evals.expected_output: The remaining work is interval-driven with no end state, so the lever check routes it to /loop, not /goal, and no checkable completion condition exists. The skill writes the save-point without a goal region, does not launch, says a background run needs a completion condition and that the user can rerun /session-flow:continue-in-background with the done condition named in the request, and falls back to the /clear-then-paste instruction.
expectations: No `claude --bg` or `claude --cloud` command runs
The message names the missing completion condition as the reason no agent was launched
The message says how to supply one: rerun /session-flow:continue-in-background with the done condition named in the request
The save-point is still written and the exit is the /clear-then-paste instruction
The message does not tell the user to type `/goal <condition>` in this session
